summary: The milestone completed 11 experiments in 1.4 minutes, with 7 classified as compute-bound. The available data ranks execution time but does not provide task-linked GPU samples or phase traces, so it cannot establish causal runtime or utilization efficiency.
bottlenecks_identified: Runtime concentration: Three-family model-local representation surface preflight was the compute-bound leader at 1.42 minutes; no phase breakdown is available to explain why.
Utilization observability gap: the GPU report provides one 0% snapshot without task linkage, so compute efficiency cannot be graded from it.
Dispatch observability gap: no data available this milestone records simultaneous model count or runner selection, so a missed DualGPURunner engagement cannot be assessed.
improvements_suggested: Emit task-scoped GPU utilization and memory samples for every compute-bound task from launch through teardown.
Record simultaneous model count and selected runner, and select DualGPURunner only when at least 2 models are loaded in parallel.
Add phase timers to the representation-surface preflight so the source of its 1.42-minute runtime can be localized.
Keep synthesis-only work outside GPU-utilization alerts.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Join compute-task start and stop timestamps to GPU utilization samples.
Persist model-count and runner-selection receipts, with conditional DualGPURunner dispatch for parallel multi-model work.
Instrument phase-level timing inside the slowest representation-surface preflight.
meta_reflection: The evidence is sufficient to rank the listed tasks but not to explain the leading runtime, grade compute-task GPU efficiency, or determine whether parallel multi-model dispatch occurred. The next milestone should capture task-correlated utilization, concurrency, runner, and phase telemetry.
